stories.title: National Champions: Team Camber Racing wins Formula Bharat 2026
stories.dek: SRMIST's Formula Student team took the combustion-category title — and first place in seven events.

facts.label: Event wins
facts.value: Endurance · Skidpad · Autocross · Acceleration · Engineering Design · Fuel Economy · Sustainability & Best Practices

facts.label: Team
facts.value: Mechanical, electrical, electronics and computing students

body: Team Camber Racing were crowned National Champions at Formula Bharat 2026 in the combustion category.

They finished first in Endurance, Skidpad, Autocross, Acceleration, Engineering Design, Fuel Economy, and Sustainability & Best Practices, and chief race driver M. Sakthiprasad took the Best Driver Award.
The team is multidisciplinary, bringing together mechanical, electrical, electronics and computing students, led by captain Himanshu Kumar (ECE, final year).

stories.title: Distinguished Winner, Apple Swift Student Challenge 2026
stories.dek: Shourya Thakur, a pre-final-year B.Tech Computer Science student, was named a Distinguished Winner of Apple's Swift Student Challenge 2026 — the first from SRMIST.
body: Shourya Thakur was named a Distinguished Winner in Apple's Swift Student Challenge 2026 — one of 50 worldwide, and the first SRMIST student to receive the honour.

His winning app, PurlStead, is an iPad playground app that helps with early screening for Parkinson's disease. It uses AI to study a user's hand movements, and all the analysis happens on the device, so no data leaves the iPad.
Apple flew him to Apple Park for WWDC 2026. He was mentored at SRMIST's iOS Development Centre.

stories.title: Paperplane: digital clinics on WhatsApp
stories.dek: Started by SRMIST School of Computing students, Paperplane helps doctors run their practice on WhatsApp.
body: Paperplane sets up digital clinics on WhatsApp, so doctors and hospitals can launch and grow their practice on the messaging app patients already use.
It automates clinical work such as appointment scheduling, prescriptions and follow-ups.
Its co-founders include Devansh Swarup and Varun Goel, who started it while students at SRMIST's School of Computing. It has raised ₹3 crore in a round led by Cornerstone Venture Partners Fund.

stories.title: SRMIST × Volvo Group: Volvo's first university-based Vehicle Technology Centre
stories.dek: Volvo Group's first Vehicle Technology Centre at a university is at SRMIST.
body: SRMIST and Volvo Group have set up Volvo's first university-based Vehicle Technology Centre.

Set up with Volvo Group CSR Trust India, it includes a Centre of Excellence in Virtual Vehicle Technologies. The aim is to bridge classroom learning and industry practice through hands-on training, collaborative research and exposure to advanced automotive technology.
